However, understanding how multi-factor authentication (MFA) works and the common methods used to target it is essential for defending your own digital identity. From a cybersecurity perspective, it is much more valuable to understand the vulnerabilities so you can better protect yourself.How MFA is Typically Targeted (Defensive Overview)Security professionals study "bypass" techniques to build more resilient systems. Most successful attacks on MFA don't "break" the encryption; instead, they exploit human behavior or technical weaknesses in specific MFA methods.Social Engineering (MFA Fatigue): Attackers may trigger dozens of push notifications to a target's phone, hoping the user will eventually click "Approve" just to make the alerts stop.Session Hijacking: Instead of bypassing the login, attackers use "infostealer" malware to snatch "session cookies" from a browser after a user has already logged in. This allows them to clone the active session on their own machine.SIM Swapping: This involves tricking a mobile carrier into porting a target's phone number to a SIM card controlled by the attacker, allowing them to intercept SMS-based verification codes.Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) Phishing: Attackers set up a proxy website that looks identical to a real login page. When the user enters their credentials and MFA code, the proxy captures them in real-time and passes them to the actual service to gain access.How to Strengthen Your Own MFATo protect your accounts against these types of threats, security experts generally recommend the following "Best Practices" hierarchy:Use Hardware Security Keys: Devices like YubiKeys are the gold standard. Because they require a physical touch and use the FIDO2 protocol, they are virtually immune to remote phishing and AiTM attacks.Use Authenticator Apps: Apps like Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator are significantly more secure than SMS, as they aren't vulnerable to SIM swapping.Enable "Number Matching": If using push notifications, ensure "number matching" is enabled. This requires you to type a number shown on the login screen into the app, preventing accidental approvals from "MFA fatigue."Protect Your Cookies: Regularly clear your browser cache and use reputable antivirus software to prevent malware from stealing your active login sessions.</ol
